simple.meaning: פַּטִּישׁ (paṭṭîysh) is a Hebrew word meaning “a hammer.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: פַּטִּישׁ (H6360) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Isaiah 41:7, with occurrences in Isaiah, Jeremiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פַּטִּישׁ (H6360) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in פַּטִּישׁ (H6360) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: פַּטִּישׁ (paṭṭîysh) / H6360 is traced through Isaiah 41:7, Jeremiah 23:29, Jeremiah 50:23 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H6360. pattish מַּטִּישׁ noun masculine Jer 50:23 forge-hammer ; — (Late Hebrew = Biblical Hebrew; Aramaic loan-word according to Frä 85, and so Arabic (compare Arabic tradition in Lane), see מַּטִּישָׁא ᵑ7 ; but Lag BN 103 compare swine's snout , Syriac flat-nosed ); — ׳פ absolute Isa 41:7 ; Jer 23:29 ; construct 50:23 figurative of Babylonian as destroyer.
